findings.highlight: chance to talk with Zouken one-on-one
findings.evidenceJa: 臓硯と一対一で向かい合えるチャンス
findings.governingReading: Shirou may never again have a chance to face Zouken one-on-one.
findings.explanation: The English narrows direct confrontation to conversation.

findings.highlight: I don’t really have a choice
findings.evidenceJa: こっちには余裕なんてない
findings.governingReading: Shirou has no time or margin to spare.
findings.explanation: The English changes urgency into lack of options.

findings.highlight: Before I know it, Assassin has vanished
findings.evidenceJa: 一切の気配を立てず消え去っていた
findings.governingReading: Assassin vanishes without producing the slightest presence, just as he appeared.
findings.explanation: The English omits the supernatural stealth of the disappearance.

findings.highlight: the Matou household
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐邸へ
findings.governingReading: Shirou heads to the Matou estate.
findings.explanation: The English changes the physical destination into a family unit.

findings.highlight: the house is filled with an ominous air
findings.evidenceJa: 日中だというのに不吉な気配
findings.governingReading: Despite it being daytime, the mansion feels ominous under the dim sky.
findings.explanation: The English omits the daytime contrast.

findings.highlight: Emiya’s successor
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮の小倅
findings.governingReading: Zouken addresses Shirou contemptuously as Emiya’s young whelp or brat.
findings.explanation: The English invents succession and removes the insult.

findings.highlight: I feel no hostility from Zouken
findings.evidenceJa: 臓硯に殺意はない
findings.governingReading: Zouken displays no intent to kill Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English changes a specific lethal intention into general hostility.

findings.highlight: confident in his ability to kill me at any time
findings.evidenceJa: 俺一人、いまさら殺す気などないって余裕
findings.governingReading: Zouken’s composure shows contemptuous lack of interest in killing Shirou alone at this stage.
findings.explanation: The English reverses absence of intent into confidence in constant ability.

findings.highlight: I can’t hide my anger
findings.evidenceJa: 敵意を隠す事は出来ない
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot conceal his hostility toward Zouken.
findings.explanation: The English changes directed hostile intent into anger as emotion.

findings.highlight: I’ll kill this monster
findings.evidenceJa: この妖怪を打ち倒す
findings.governingReading: Shirou resolves to strike Zouken down before he is killed.
findings.explanation: The English promotes defeat into explicit killing.

findings.highlight: before anything can happen
findings.evidenceJa: 殺される前に
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s narrow condition is acting before Zouken’s Servants kill him.
findings.explanation: The English removes the mortal threat and replaces it with anything happening.

findings.highlight: She will die
findings.evidenceJa: アレが自滅する
findings.governingReading: Zouken claims Sakura will self-destruct even if the worms are removed.
findings.explanation: The English removes the specific self-destruction mechanism.

findings.highlight: What did you do to her
findings.evidenceJa: 桜は一体
findings.governingReading: Shirou begins demanding what Sakura actually is.
findings.explanation: The English changes the interrupted ontological question into what Zouken did.

findings.highlight: put shape to the soul
findings.evidenceJa: 魂の物質化
findings.governingReading: Makiri’s objective is the materialization of the soul, described as true immortality.
findings.explanation: The English weakens a technical conversion into vaguely giving shape.

findings.highlight: after the war ten years ago
findings.evidenceJa: 十年前の戦いの折
findings.governingReading: Zouken says he gave Sakura Grail functions during the war ten years earlier.
findings.explanation: The English moves the intervention to after the war.

findings.highlight: I embedded the Holy Grail within her
findings.evidenceJa: 回収した聖杯を移植した
findings.governingReading: Zouken says he transplanted the recovered Grail into Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English omits recovery provenance and weakens transplantation to embedding.

findings.highlight: I made sure she can function as a human
findings.evidenceJa: 桜が人間として生活できるよう工夫はした
findings.governingReading: Zouken claims he devised measures allowing Sakura to live as a human being.
findings.explanation: The English reduces human life to functional operation.

findings.highlight: about an eighth my own way
findings.evidenceJa: 八割がた自己流
findings.governingReading: Zouken says roughly eighty percent of his imitation was improvised in his own fashion.
findings.explanation: The English changes eighty percent into one eighth, reversing the scale of his technical deviation.

findings.highlight: her body became a container to receive the souls. It became a tool catalyst to become the gate when the ritual is completed
findings.evidenceJa: 肉体は魂を受け入れる為の聖杯となり、儀式が果たされた時、門となって道を繋げる触媒となった
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s body first becomes the Grail-vessel that receives the soul and, upon completion of the ritual, the catalyst that serves as a gate and connects the path.
findings.explanation: The English breaks the staged relation among vessel, gate, catalyst, and path, and its conditional branches leave a malformed causal sentence.

findings.highlight: He laughs
findings.evidenceJa: 呵々、と愉快げに笑う
findings.governingReading: Zouken laughs heartily and with evident amusement.
findings.explanation: The English removes the pleasure coloring his response to Shirou’s horror.

findings.highlight: heir to Emiya
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮の小倅
findings.governingReading: Zouken again calls Shirou Emiya’s young whelp.
findings.explanation: The English invents a formal succession role and removes the belittling address.

findings.highlight: lives as a human
findings.evidenceJa: 天寿を全うするように施した
findings.governingReading: Zouken claims he arranged for Sakura to live as a human and complete her natural lifespan.
findings.explanation: The English drops the claimed lifespan limit, which defines the experiment’s originally intended pace.

findings.highlight: the function to collect souls
findings.evidenceJa: 魂を収める器としての機能
findings.governingReading: Sakura was designed to function as a vessel that contains souls.
findings.explanation: The English changes containment in a vessel into the active collection of souls.

findings.highlight: a ritual dedicated to that end
findings.evidenceJa: その座に至る為の儀式
findings.governingReading: The Holy Grail War was established as a ritual for reaching that Seat or state.
findings.explanation: The English removes the destination concept and reduces it to an unspecified end.

findings.highlight: I am the only one who still lives
findings.evidenceJa: ワシだけが今も無様に生き続けておる
findings.governingReading: Zouken says he alone still continues his unsightly or disgraceful life.
findings.explanation: The English removes his self-characterizing acknowledgment of the manner of his survival.

findings.highlight: To use the Matou successor to achieve our goal in the far future
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐の後継者たちによって、遥か先になるであろう悲願達成の為に
findings.governingReading: The distant objective was to be achieved by generations of Matou successors.
findings.explanation: The English turns plural successors into one successor and recasts their agency as Zouken using that person.

findings.highlight: Sakura was prepared to be an unadaptable Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 本来なら“適応しない聖杯”だったはずの桜
findings.governingReading: Sakura was originally expected to be a Grail that would not adapt.
findings.explanation: The English changes an expected limitation into an intentional preparation.

findings.highlight: she still live in spite of taking in so many Servants
findings.evidenceJa: 多くのサーヴァントを取り込みながらも自滅せず
findings.governingReading: Sakura has absorbed many Servants without self-destructing.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the specific failure mode of self-destruction to continued survival and is grammatically damaged.

findings.highlight: Forgetting the possibility of Assassin’s intervention
findings.evidenceJa: 臓硯が従えているアサシンの事も忘れ
findings.governingReading: Shirou forgets about Assassin, whom Zouken commands.
findings.explanation: The English turns a commanded Servant and a categorical lapse into only the possibility of intervention.

findings.highlight: something that only sacrifices human lives
findings.evidenceJa: 人間を犠牲にしただけのモノ
findings.governingReading: Shirou condemns the object as something produced merely by sacrificing a human being.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes and generalizes the sacrifice, weakening the immediate reference to Sakura.

findings.highlight: My body wobbles back
findings.evidenceJa: 踏み出した体が、後ろによろめく
findings.governingReading: The body that had stepped forward staggers backward.
findings.explanation: The English removes the reversal from advance to recoil.

findings.highlight: My upraised arm falls
findings.evidenceJa: 振り上げた拳が落ちる
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s raised fist drops.
findings.explanation: The English changes the aggression-bearing fist into his whole arm.

findings.highlight: in place of anger
findings.evidenceJa: 臓硯に対する敵意より先に
findings.governingReading: Regret overwhelms Shirou before his hostility toward Zouken can.
findings.explanation: The English replaces directed hostility with generic anger and changes the temporal relation into substitution.

findings.highlight: I calmed it down every night
findings.evidenceJa: 毎夜なだめていたようなもの
findings.governingReading: What Zouken did was akin to placating the shadow every night.
findings.explanation: The English promotes his analogy and self-serving characterization into a literal repeated action.

findings.highlight: My heart thumps loudly
findings.evidenceJa: 心臓が痙攣する
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s heart convulses.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes an ordinary loud heartbeat for a violent bodily spasm.

findings.highlight: open a gate
findings.evidenceJa: 外に通じる“孔”を開く
findings.governingReading: The three families sought to open a hole leading outside the world; the surface reading is hole and the ruby reads gate.
findings.explanation: The English keeps only gate and removes the cosmological outside relation and the written-reading layer.

findings.highlight: a gate to connect this world to a world where every wish comes true
findings.evidenceJa: “あらゆる望みが叶う場所”とこちらの世界を繋げる門
findings.governingReading: The completed Grail is a gate connecting this world to the place where every wish can be granted.
findings.explanation: The English promotes the destination into another world and changes potential fulfillment into automatic occurrence.

findings.highlight: I do not mind if she dies from her own carelessness
findings.evidenceJa: その不始末で自分が壊れるのは勝手
findings.governingReading: Zouken says she may break herself through that failure if she wishes.
findings.explanation: The English changes bodily or functional destruction into death and adds personal carelessness as blame.

findings.highlight: the Holy Grail I made
findings.evidenceJa: ワシが手塩にかけた聖杯
findings.governingReading: Zouken calls Sakura the Grail he painstakingly raised and tended.
findings.explanation: The English removes the cultivation language central to his possessive view of her.

findings.highlight: You should recognize the similarities between them
findings.evidenceJa: 身近にいたおぬしならば、アレと桜が似ていると判っていた筈
findings.governingReading: Zouken grounds Shirou’s expected recognition in his having been close to Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English removes the relationship that makes Shirou especially able and responsible to recognize the resemblance.

findings.highlight: I have to accept that the crime is Sakura’s as well
findings.evidenceJa: その罪は、桜に及ぶのだと認めなく、て、は
findings.governingReading: Shirou forces himself to acknowledge that the shadow’s guilt or consequences extend to Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English converts a deliberately relational statement into direct ownership of the crime by Sakura.

findings.highlight: it took Sakura’s form and imitated existence in this plane
findings.evidenceJa: 桜を原型にし、こちら側での存在を象ったモノ
findings.governingReading: When emerging through Sakura as the gate, the shadow uses her as its prototype and models a form of existence on this side.
findings.explanation: The English turns the prototype relation into simply taking her form and renders the shadow as imitating existence itself.

findings.highlight: the shadow does not want me going near her. It does not have a will of its own
findings.evidenceJa: あの影はワシが桜に近寄る事を阻む。意思こそないものの
findings.governingReading: The shadow prevents Zouken from approaching Sakura despite possessing no will of its own.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the shadow a desire immediately before denying that it has a will.

findings.highlight: I cannot control her, as I have been cut off from her
findings.evidenceJa: 桜と離れたこの体では、アレを律する事はできん
findings.governingReading: Zouken says that with this body separated from Sakura, he cannot regulate the shadow.
findings.explanation: The English removes the bodily qualifier, changes regulating the shadow into controlling Sakura, and recasts bodily separation as Zouken personally being cut off from her.

findings.highlight: the crest worm
findings.evidenceJa: 体内の刻印虫
findings.governingReading: Shirou thinks of dealing with the Crest Worms inside Sakura’s body.
findings.explanation: The English again reduces the infestation to one worm.

findings.highlight: I have never used the crest worm
findings.evidenceJa: 刻印虫を使った覚えなどない
findings.governingReading: Zouken evasively says he has no recollection of using the Crest Worms.
findings.explanation: The English strengthens a memory-framed denial into a categorical claim that he never used one.

findings.highlight: endure the strong onflow
findings.evidenceJa: その奔流に耐えられる筈もなかろう
findings.governingReading: Zouken calls the incoming magical power a torrent that Sakura’s mind cannot withstand.
findings.explanation: The English weakens the force image and uses the malformed or highly unnatural “strong onflow.”

findings.highlight: the Holy Grail should appear
findings.evidenceJa: 無意識を借り受けていた聖杯が浮上する
findings.governingReading: The Grail that had been borrowing Sakura’s unconscious will rise to the surface when her consciousness empties.
findings.explanation: The English omits both the borrowed-unconscious relation and the directional emergence.

findings.highlight: It is meaningless to kill me here
findings.evidenceJa: ここでワシを倒すのも無駄なこと
findings.governingReading: Zouken says defeating him here would be useless.
findings.explanation: The English again narrows defeat into killing.

findings.highlight: The timing to open the gate, the completion of the Great Holy Grail, does not last long
findings.evidenceJa: 大聖杯の完成……門を開く時期、というものはそう長くは続かぬ
findings.governingReading: The completed Greater Grail has a limited period or window in which the gate can open.
findings.explanation: The English reverses the apposition between completion and the gate-opening period, leaving the mechanism unclear.

findings.highlight: I can’t really hear his question
findings.evidenceJa: 老魔術師の問いは、よく聞こえなかった
findings.governingReading: In Shirou’s reeling state, the old magus’s question does not properly register.
findings.explanation: The English makes this a literal failure of hearing.

findings.highlight: Can I save Sakura?
findings.evidenceJa: 桜を救えるのか、と奥歯を噛む
findings.governingReading: Shirou grinds his back teeth as he frames the question of saving Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English omits the bodily strain closing the thought.

findings.highlight: she will gladly give her life if it’s for you
findings.evidenceJa: 桜は喜んでその判断に身を委ねよう
findings.governingReading: Zouken predicts that Sakura will gladly entrust herself to Shirou’s judgment.
findings.explanation: The English turns submission to his decision into an explicit willingness to die for him, preempting the very choice Zouken is manipulating.

findings.highlight: Ending one evil life to save thousands
findings.evidenceJa: 万人の為に悪を討つ
findings.governingReading: Zouken invokes striking down evil for the sake of all people.
findings.explanation: The English changes the universal scope into a numerical crowd.

findings.highlight: Ending one evil life to save thousands
findings.evidenceJa: 万人の為に悪を討つ
findings.governingReading: Zouken formulates Kiritsugu’s ideal as striking down evil for everyone.
findings.explanation: The English inserts the death of one person and directly maps the maxim onto Sakura before the next sentence identifies her as Shirou’s enemy.

findings.highlight: the distorted hallway
findings.evidenceJa: 飴のようにぐにゃぐにゃに曲がりくねった廊下
findings.governingReading: To Shirou, the corridor twists and bends limply like candy.
findings.explanation: The English removes the grotesque soft-material simile.

findings.highlight: I don’t feel anything even when I walk or lean against the wall
findings.evidenceJa: 床を踏む足も、壁によりかかる手も、確かな感触など何もなかった
findings.governingReading: Neither the feet stepping on the floor nor the hand leaning against the wall gives Shirou any definite sensation.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes the precise body-to-surface contacts and changes absence of definite sensation into feeling nothing at all.

findings.highlight: It’s ugly
findings.evidenceJa: 酷い
findings.governingReading: Shirou judges the experience or situation as awful.
findings.explanation: The English turns general horror into visual ugliness.

findings.highlight: this is fate
findings.evidenceJa: これも運命と諦めて貰おう
findings.governingReading: Zouken says Sakura will have to resign herself to this as fate.
findings.explanation: The English removes his coercive demand that Sakura accept her death.

findings.highlight: a hollow being, like a mere puppet
findings.evidenceJa: ただそこに在るだけの人形が如き虚ろな存在
findings.governingReading: Zouken describes Sakura as a hollow puppet-like existence that merely remained there.
findings.explanation: The English drops the stasis of merely existing, part of his dehumanizing construction of her past.

findings.highlight: I stumble towards my house
findings.evidenceJa: 崩れそうな足を進ませた
findings.governingReading: Shirou forces forward legs that feel about to collapse.
findings.explanation: The English reduces impending bodily collapse to a stumble.

findings.highlight: It’s not good to let Tohsaka or Sakura know about it
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂にも[line3]眠っている桜にも良くはない
findings.governingReading: Shirou specifies both Rin and the sleeping Sakura as people who should not learn of the meeting.
findings.explanation: The English omits Sakura’s sleeping state, which explains the secrecy window.

findings.highlight: before they notice
findings.evidenceJa: 二人が俺の留守に気がつく前に
findings.governingReading: Shirou must return before the two notice his absence.
findings.explanation: The English leaves what they might notice unstated.

findings.highlight: I chose to be with Sakura
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の味方になると決めた
findings.governingReading: Shirou decided to become Sakura’s ally rather than an ally of justice.
findings.explanation: The English weakens a morally charged allegiance into being with her.

findings.highlight: another disaster to occur, taking hundreds of lives
findings.evidenceJa: 多くの命を奪った、あの惨劇
findings.governingReading: The earlier catastrophe took many lives.
findings.explanation: The English invents a numerical scale of hundreds.

findings.highlight: It is like denying myself
findings.evidenceJa: 自分自身を否定する事に他ならない
findings.governingReading: Breaking the oath would be nothing other than denying Shirou’s own self.
findings.explanation: The English weakens identity-level equivalence into a comparison.

findings.highlight: You will be rejected by everything that has supported you until now
findings.evidenceJa: 今までおまえを支えてきたモノが、おまえ自身を否定する
findings.governingReading: The thing that has supported Shirou until now would itself deny him.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes the supporting principle and converts its internal moral contradiction into passive external rejection.

findings.highlight: Your crime will never be forgiven
findings.evidenceJa: 死の際において。その罪が、許される事はなくなるだろう
findings.governingReading: Whatever the outcome, Shirou imagines that at the moment of death the guilt will no longer be forgivable.
findings.explanation: The English removes the deathbed frame governing the judgment.

findings.highlight: innocent people who will be killed
findings.evidenceJa: 無関係に命を奪われる者
findings.governingReading: People uninvolved in the conflict will have their lives taken tonight.
findings.explanation: The English changes relational noninvolvement into a moral verdict of innocence.

findings.highlight: You are no different than the cause of the fire that day
findings.evidenceJa: 自ら火を放ったのと変わらない
findings.governingReading: Shirou accuses himself of being no different from having personally set the fire that day.
findings.explanation: The English removes the imagined act of arson and makes him equivalent to an abstract cause.

findings.highlight: to protect one person
findings.evidenceJa: たった一人を生かそうというのなら
findings.governingReading: The internal accusation frames Shirou’s choice as keeping a single person alive.
findings.explanation: The English recasts preservation of Sakura’s life as general protection.
